name: SequenceTree Turn Mode
description: Decides per prompt which research-suite hooks and gates run: skip, light, research, code or deep

classify.label: What kind of turn is this?

config.instructions: Classify the user's prompt (state.prompt) in a coding session on SequenceTree, a C++ JUCE plugin. Pick the one option that describes what the user is asking for in this message. A prompt that asks for code to be written or changed is code or deep even if it also asks a question. A prompt that only asks about code, research, or a plan is research. Short replies and conversational steering are control.

options.label: A control command that steers the conversation without asking for new work: stop, wait, hurry up, move on, continue, go ahead, yes, no, or a short reply to a question
A simple question or basic command that can be answered directly, without reading through or changing code
A research, analysis, explanation, review or planning question: understanding how code works, comparing approaches, looking something up, or writing a plan, with no code being written or changed
A routine request to write, generate, change, fix, rename, refactor or delete code
An in-depth coding request: a new feature, a change across several files or classes, an audio-thread or traversal change, or a design question about how code should be structured

config.description: No gates and no extra checks for this turn.
config.directive: Do what the command says. Run no design-rule, readability or systematic checks.
Answer directly. No rule recitation, no audit and no gates; the Key Design Rules still bind any code written.
Answer from the real code: name the actual functions, files and call sites. Do not run the design-rule or readability gates; no code is being changed.

config.description: Full protocol: gates plus the change trees at Stop.
config.directive: Run the full verification protocol: the design-rule audit now, and the change trees on the diff when the turn ends. Edit Source/ and Tests/ through the refactor.* commands: refactor.edit for text edits (exact, '<<< all', '<<< regex', '<<< after' / '<<< before', --build), refactor.rewrite for one shape at many sites, refactor.encap / decap / replace for extract, inline and rename, Write for a new file. A Python script, sed -i, redirect or copy that writes into them is denied.
